correctness.rationale: Canonical alternating blocks of every acyclic K_{m,n} orientation are unique. An edge is flippable exactly across consecutive blocks, giving degree sum_i |W_i||W_{i+1}|. Their blow-up path is connected and has the minimum m+n−1 edges exactly when every internal block is a singleton. Counting even- and odd-length sequences gives the displayed falling-factorial simple-vertex formula, including the star and balanced boundaries. Independently, 2-by-n binary matrices forbid simultaneous 01 and 10 columns, yielding the closed binomial degree polynomial; the balanced-family limit follows by an explicit count of a subset of orientations. Two standalone checkers reproduce degree polynomials for small parameters using independent representations. No infinite claim rests on finite computation.

value.rationale: Simple vertices of a graphical zonotope are intrinsic structural invariants, and the exact count for all complete-bipartite cases identifies when the local orientation-flip graph has the smallest possible branching degree. The K_{2,n} formula computes the entire degree distribution, not an arbitrary isolated coefficient, and establishes exponential rarity of simple orientations. The theorem ties a classical poly-Bernoulli object to local geometric simplicity and resolves a natural enumeration beyond known totals or individual flip tests.
